item.content:encoded:
The University of the Sunshine Coast (UniSC) in Australia is offering a wide range of exciting scholarship opportunities for international students commencing in 2025. These scholarships are designed to attract talented students from around the globe, reduce the financial burden of tuition, and support academic excellence. Whether you’re applying for an undergraduate or postgraduate program, UniSC provides valuable financial assistance through competitive scholarship programs.

UniSC’s scholarship offerings in 2025 include tuition fee reductions of up to 20%, with automatic consideration for many applicants. The university is located in Queensland, one of Australia’s most beautiful and innovative regions, offering students a safe, modern, and enriching learning environment. You can also apply for the Kochi University of Technology Scholarship 2026 in Japan | Fully Funded

University of the Sunshine Coast Scholarships 2025 Details:

  • Host Country: Australia
  • University: University of the Sunshine Coast (UniSC)
  • Study Level: Undergraduate and Postgraduate
  • Eligible Candidates: International Students

Benefits of UniSC Scholarships 2025:

1. International Student Scholarship

  • 15% tuition fee reduction
  • Automatically applied to all eligible international students commencing in 2025

2. English Excellence Scholarship

  • 20% tuition fee reduction
  • Awarded to students who exceed English language test score requirements (IELTS, TOEFL iBT, or PTE)
  • Requires application via an education agent or an international admissions officer

3. International Bright Futures Scholarship

  • 20% tuition fee reduction
  • Available for students enrolling in newly launched programs:
    • Bachelor of Education Studies (Early Childhood)
    • Master of Business Intelligence and Analytics
    • MBA / Master of Business Intelligence and Analytics (dual degree)
  • Automatically applied upon offer acceptance

4. UniSC Asylum Seeker Scholarship

  • Covers tuition and living costs
  • For asylum seekers on temporary visas with financial need

5. U3A Merit-Based Equity Bursary

  • For second-year and above undergraduate international students
  • Supports students involved in community service

6. Australia Awards Scholarships

  • Fully funded scholarships provided by the Australian Government
  • Includes tuition, living expenses, health insurance, and travel support
  • Available for citizens of select countries

7. Northcote Graduate Scholarship

  • For UK residents pursuing postgraduate degrees in Australia
  • Preference for those with the strong academic purpose for studying in Australia

Check University of Tasmania Scholarships 2025-2026 in Australia (Fully Funded)

Eligibility Criteria for UniSC Scholarships 2025:

  • Everyone from any nationality can apply.
  • Must be a commencing international student in 2025.
  • Must meet the program’s academic and language requirements.
  • For the English Excellence Scholarship, students must meet the minimum score criteria in IELTS, TOEFL iBT, or PTE (refer to UniSC’s official scholarship requirements table).
  • For the Bright Futures Scholarship, students must enroll in one of the eligible newly launched programs.
  • Applicants must retain international student status throughout the study duration.
  • Scholarships cannot be combined (only one UniSC scholarship can be used at a time).

Required Documents:

  • Offer letter from UniSC
  • Academic transcripts and degree certificates
  • English language proficiency test results
  • Valid passport copy
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Proof of community involvement (if applying for U3A bursary)
  • Personal statement or cover letter (if required by the specific scholarship)

Deadline:

There is no separate deadline for most UniSC scholarships as they are automatically applied with your program offer. However, individual degree program deadlines may vary, and the English Excellence Scholarship requires early application.

Check Best Government Scholarships 2025-26 Around the World

How to Apply for UniSC Scholarships 2025?

Follow these simple steps to apply:

  • Choose Your Program: Browse UniSC’s degree programs and select one that fits your goals.
  • Apply for Admission: Submit your application online via UniSC’s official admissions portal.
  • Receive Your Offer Letter: If accepted, your offer letter will include scholarship details (where applicable).
  • Apply for English Excellence (if applicable): If you meet the English test score requirements, contact your education agent or International Admissions Officer to request this scholarship.
  • Accept Your Offer: Finalize your admission and pay the required deposit.
  • Begin Your Study in Australia: Enjoy world-class education and scholarship support at UniSC!

These scholarships support graduate research degrees, enabling scholars to explore critical human rights issues through in-depth academic study. Open to both international and domestic applicants, the program aims to empower future leaders in the field.

The University of Melbourne provides a world-class academic environment and a diverse community that fosters research excellence and global collaboration.   • Living allowance of $43,500 per year (up to 2 years for Master’s, 3.5 years for PhD)
  • Full tuition fee coverage for the entire study duration

Eligibility Criteria for the Human Rights Scholarships 2025 in Australia:

Selection Criteria:

item.content:encoded:
Takoradi Technical University, TTU, through its Faculty of Business Studies, has signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, with the Chartered Institute of Financial Investment Analysts-Ghana, CIFIA-Ghana.

The MoU is to provide professional training and certification opportunities
for both staff and students pursuing accounting, banking, and finance-related programmes.

The Vice Chancellor of TTU, Rev. Prof. John Frank Eshun, expressed his support for the partnership, stating how it falls within the University’s mandate.

“I want to take this opportunity to welcome you to Takoradi Technical University. As you are aware, our mandate requires us to collaborate with professional bodies to help our students build capacity. Your presence here is a step in the right direction, and we will ensure the MoU succeeds.” he expressed.

Dean of the Faculty of Business Studies, Prof. Mrs. Abigail Gura, emphasizing the partnership’s alignment with the faculty’s vision for professional advancement, said it will not only benefit students and staff of the faculty, but the entire University.

“I believe this MoU will not only benefit the Faculty of Business Studies but the entire university. Through this partnership, there are numerous opportunities that faculty members, students, and even administrators can access. This is a professional body where acquiring a professional certificate alongside an academic degree is a significant advantage, “she said

On his part, Vice President of the Chartered Institute of Financial Investment Analysts-Ghana, Dr. Gabriel Odeh Apotey, while sharing his optimism about the collaboration during the signing ceremony, expressed confidence that the partnership would flourish and bring substantial benefits to both parties. He highlighted that students and staff who enrol under the partnership would enjoy exemptions related to fee payments and examinations.

Dr. Apotey also conferred honorary Fellowships of the institute on the Vice Chancellor and the Registrar of TTU.

The post Attitudes Hinder Growth Far More Than Lack Of Skills-McDan appeared first on Ghananewsprime.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a reason why I talk about attitude a lot. It’s pretty simple: your skill can get you any job, but your attitude will determine how long you keep it.

I’ve seen many smart individuals struggle and stagnate in their careers—not because of a lack of ability, but because their mindset held them back. It’s heartbreaking to watch potential go untapped due to feelings of entitlement, arrogance, or an unwillingness to take responsibility and accept feedback. These attitudes hinder growth far more than a lack of skill.

No one wants to work alongside someone who is gifted yet difficult. Nobody wants to work with someone who is an expert yet problematic. Your bosses, colleagues, and clients are human too; they will understand mistakes, but they seek collaboration and support.

That is why promotions don’t just go to the smartest; they also go to the most reliable, adaptable, and emotionally intelligent. Promotions go to those who not only shine in their expertise but also demonstrate trustworthiness. Your technical abilities definitely count, but your attitude plays a critical role in shaping your career journey.

Are you someone who takes initiative? Open to learning? Easy to collaborate with? Embracing these traits create a positive environment for yourself and others around you. While talent may initially catch attention, it’s your attitude that keeps you connected and valued in the long run. These things are what open doors for you.

So, invest in your attitude with kindness and understanding, nurturing it as you would any important aspect of your life. This is how you can build a fulfilling and enduring career.

It combines academic excellence with practical relevance, offering students a unique chance to enhance their leadership capabilities and development strategies in entrepreneurship and business promotion.

The DAAD EPOS SEPT Scholarship 2026 is a golden opportunity for aspiring business leaders, development professionals, and entrepreneurs from developing nations. item.content:encoded:
In the wake of Sunday night’s torrential rains that caused severe flooding in parts of the Adentan Constituency, the Member of Parliament, Hon. Mohammed Adamu Ramadan, has called for lasting solutions to the persistent flooding challenges affecting the area.

On the night of the downpour, Hon. Ramadan braved the elements and, together with the Engineers Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces, rescued several residents trapped in their homes by the rising floodwaters. His timely intervention provided much-needed relief and hope to many distressed families.

Determined to go beyond emergency response and tackle the root causes of the flooding, the MP led a high-powered delegation on Monday morning to assess the extent of the devastation. The delegation included the Minister for Works and Housing, Hon. Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) officials at the National, Regional, and Municipal levels, and the Municipal Chief Executive.

The team toured the most affected communities, engaged with residents, and gathered firsthand information to help guide coordinated efforts toward preventing future occurrences. The MP stressed the urgent need for sustainable drainage systems, improved urban planning, and continued collaboration among government agencies to safeguard lives and property. He also appealed to benevolent organisations and individuals to support the affected residents in this difficult time.

This intervention reflects Hon. Ramadan’s unwavering commitment to the welfare of his constituents and his resolve to ensure that no community is left behind during times of crisis. As Adentan begins the recovery process, the MP has assured residents that he, together with the Municipal Assembly, will continue to advocate for lasting solutions to the flooding menace.

He further called on residents to refrain from building on waterways, noting that such practices significantly contribute to the recurring floods and must be curtailed to prevent future disasters.

item.content:encoded:
Looking for part-time jobs in the UK as an international student in 2025? Explore exciting opportunities that align with your schedule and skillset. With a diverse range of industries and flexible work options, international students can find rewarding positions to support their studies and gain valuable experience. From retail and hospitality to tutoring and freelance gigs, the UK offers a wealth of part-time employment prospects tailored to students’ needs and interests.

Securing a part-time job in the UK can enhance your academic journey while providing financial stability. Stay updated on job boards, university career centers, and networking events to discover the latest openings. Highlight your unique qualifications and international perspective to stand out to potential employers. By balancing work and studies effectively, international students can make the most of their time in the UK, both academically and professionally.

With a strong focus on diversity and inclusivity, the UK job market welcomes international students seeking part-time employment opportunities in 2025. Leverage your cultural background and language skills to excel in customer-facing roles or multicultural environments. Additionally, explore remote work options and online platforms for flexibility and convenience. By staying proactive and adaptable, international students can embark on a fulfilling part-time job journey in the UK while broadening their horizons and building valuable connections.

Benefits of Working While Studying in UK:

  • Financial Independence: Part-time work provides students with the opportunity to earn money to cover living expenses, tuition fees, and other costs associated with studying abroad, reducing reliance on family or loans.
  • Skill Development: Part-time jobs allow students to develop valuable skills such as time management, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving, enhancing their employability upon graduation.
  • Cultural Immersion: Engaging in part-time work exposes students to the local culture, customs, and workplace practices, facilitating integration into the UK society and broadening their worldview.
  • Networking Opportunities: Working in various industries enables students to build professional networks, connect with potential employers, and discover career paths aligned with their interests and aspirations.
  • Enhanced CV/Resume: Part-time work experience enhances students’ CVs/resumes, demonstrating their work ethic, initiative, and adaptability to future employers, making them more competitive in the job market.
  • Improved Language Skills: Working in English-speaking environments helps students improve their language proficiency, communication skills, and confidence, which are valuable assets in both academic and professional settings.
  • Time Management: Balancing work commitments with academic studies teaches students valuable time management skills, enabling them to prioritize tasks effectively and maintain a healthy work-life balance.
  • Personal Growth: Working while studying fosters personal growth and independence, empowering students to take ownership of their finances, career development, and overall well-being.

Check Poland Work Visa 2025 (Application Process)

Part-time work in UK regulations and guidelines:

Understanding the rules and regulations regarding part-time work for international students on a UK student visa is crucial. Here’s what you need to know:

  • Part-time work limits: Full-time students are allowed to work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during university breaks. However, students pursuing a degree can only work 10 hours per week while studying full-time.
  • Break period regulations: During session breaks, you can take up a job for up to 40 hours per week, allowing for more flexibility with your schedule. This typically translates to 8 hours a day with weekends off.
  • Restrictions on freelance and contract work: International students are not permitted to engage in freelance or contract work. Employment should be within the constraints of part-time roles and not as a full-time employee without a post-study work visa.
  • Work-study balance: It’s essential to maintain a balance between work and studies. Your employment should not adversely affect your academic performance. Prioritize your education while managing your part-time job commitments effectively.

Types of Part-Time Jobs

When seeking part-time jobs in the UK as an international student, understanding the types of opportunities available is essential. Here’s a breakdown of the two major categories:

On-Campus Jobs:

  • On-campus jobs are situated within university premises, offering convenience for students.
  • Opportunities can be found in various university departments such as the library, computer labs, reception, gym, and cafeteria.
  • These roles are highly sought after due to their proximity and flexible scheduling, but they may be limited in availability.

Off-Campus Jobs:

  • Off-campus jobs provide a wider range of opportunities but may require commuting.
  • Roles include office support, receptionist positions, waiter/waitress jobs, call center positions, and data entry roles.
  • Students typically need permission from their universities to engage in off-campus part-time work.

Part-Time Online Jobs:

  • Online part-time jobs offer flexibility and convenience, allowing students to work from anywhere with an internet connection.
  • Opportunities include freelance work, remote customer service roles, content writing, graphic design, and virtual assistant positions.
  • Online jobs can complement a rigorous course load and provide valuable work experience.

Exploring both on-campus and off-campus options, as well as online opportunities, provides international students with a diverse range of part-time job prospects to support their studies and enhance their skill set while studying in the UK.

Best Part-Time Jobs in UK & Their Average Pay:

Retail & Customer-Facing Roles

  • Retail Worker: £13.90/hour

How to Find Part-Time Jobs in UK?

Finding part-time jobs in the UK as an international student can be facilitated through various channels. Here’s a guide on how to find these opportunities:

  • University Career Services: Most universities in the UK have dedicated career services that assist students in finding part-time jobs, internships, and work placements. Visit your university’s career center or website for job listings, workshops, and career fairs.
  • Online Job Portals: Utilize online job portals and websites specifically designed for part-time job seekers in the UK. Popular platforms include Indeed, Reed, Totaljobs, and StudentJob. Filter your search by location, job type, and industry to find suitable opportunities.
  • University Job Boards: Many universities have their own job boards or online platforms where local businesses and employers post part-time job vacancies targeted at students. Check your university’s website or bulletin boards on campus for job listings.
  • Networking: Networking is a valuable tool for finding part-time jobs. Connect with fellow students, professors, alumni, and professionals in your field of interest. Attend networking events, seminars, and industry meet-ups to expand your network and discover job opportunities through referrals.
  • Local Businesses: Visit local businesses, shops, restaurants, cafes, and bars in your university town or city center to inquire about part-time job openings. Drop off your CV/resume and express your interest in working part-time.
  • Recruitment Agencies: Consider registering with recruitment agencies that specialize in placing students and young professionals in part-time or temporary roles. These agencies can help match your skills and preferences with suitable job opportunities.
  • Online Freelancing Platforms: Explore online freelancing platforms such as Upwork, Freelancer, and Fiverr to find remote freelance gigs in various fields such as writing, graphic design, programming, and digital marketing.
  • Social Media: Follow job-related hashtags and groups on social media platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, and Twitter to stay updated on part-time job opportunities, networking events, and industry news.
  • Job Fairs and Events: Attend local job fairs, career expos, and recruitment events organized by universities, businesses, and job agencies. These events provide opportunities to meet employers, submit resumes, and participate in on-the-spot interviews.

item.content:encoded:
The newly constituted Governing Board of the National Service Authority (NSA) has been officially inaugurated today at the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment in Accra.

The 15-member board is chaired by Emmanuel Okai Mintah and comprises key representatives from various ministries, institutions, and the private sector.

Members of the board include Dr James Asare Adjei from the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI), Felix Gyamfi, Director-General of the NSA, Cecilia Sheitu Nyadia from the Ministry of Technology and Innovation, Colonel Frederick Aboagye Kasapa from the Ministry of Defence, and Dr Wisdom Atiwoto from the Ministry of Health.

Members

Other members are Emma Ofori Agyemang from the Ministry of Youth Development, Kwabena Denkyira from the Ministry of Local Government, Paul Siamen from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, Shadrack Mensah from the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations, and Matilda Azumah from the Ministry of Education, as well as two presidential nominees—Henrietta Asante and Elorm Goh.

Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama, the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, Hon. George Opare-Addo, charged the board to demonstrate innovation, efficiency, and accountability in managing the affairs of the Authority.

He urged them to address persistent issues such as the presence of ghost names in the system and to create an environment that enables service personnel to acquire hands-on experience relevant to today’s dynamic job market.

President’s vision

He noted the president’s vision of developing graduates who are disciplined and eager to serve the nation with dedication and integrity.

The Board Chair, Emmanuel Okai Mintah, expressed appreciation to the President for the confidence reposed in him and pledged to work tirelessly to position the NSA as a world-class institution that delivers practical solutions to national challenges.

Meanwhile, the Director-General of NSA, Felix Gyamfi, expressed confidence that the new board will inject fresh energy and direction to elevate the Authority’s impact and operational effectiveness.
